FUEL PATHWAYS DESCRIPTION B.1 SOYBEAN/UCO | TRANSESTERIFICATION | BIODIESEL Transesterification is a commercialized technology (TRL = 9) for biodiesel production. In the United States, most biodiesel (BD) is produced from vegetable oil and animal fats. Some low- value feedstocks, such as used cooking oil (UCO) and distillers corn oil (DCO) are becoming prevalent but will require additional feedstock treatment steps (Xu et al., 2022). In this study, TEA was conducted for BD produced from soybean oil to represent the current state of technology. In this process, refined soybean oil, methanol, and sodium methylate are fed to the reactor to be converted to fatty acid methyl ester (FAME). The reactor output is sent to a gravity decanter to be separated into FAME phase and glycerin phase. The FAME phase is sent to a second reactor to complete the transesterification reaction. The FAME product is washed with water and then distilled under vacuum to produce the final BD product. Glycerin is sold as a byproduct that is widely used in wound and burn treatment. B.2 SOYBEAN/UCO | HYDROPROCESSING | RD Hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) fuel is another commercially available biofuel (TRL = 9). The HEFA process uses the same feedstock as the BD process (Xu et al., 2022). Similarly, soybean oil is selected as the feedstock in this TEA study.
